# Kailash OS Cookbook {#cookbook-home}

This book is the task-oriented companion to the [Kailash OS
guide](https://docs.kailash.tools). The project home — release notes,
the paper, the roadmap — is [kailash.site](https://kailash.site).
The guide explains what each tool is. Its pages follow the man-style
reference form for the whole catalogue. The cookbook answers
**how to do X**: every page is a standalone recipe in the O'Reilly
cookbook format —

1. **Problem** — the task, in operator terms
2. **Solution** — the ready-to-run commands with expected output
   shapes
3. **Discussion** — why it works, what it touches, when to choose an
   alternative
4. **See also** — the matching reference pages and neighbour recipes

Recipes are worked runs, never invented transcripts. Output renders
as *shapes* with placeholders. An unfinished step renders as an
explicit `PENDING` marker. This follows the no-invented-evidence rule
used across the project documents.

## How the book is organised

- **Sections are themes** — Getting started / Scanning / Attack–defence
  pairs / Ops / Administrator. A recipe never moves between sections.
- **Level is metadata, not navigation** — each recipe carries an
  easy/medium/hard level in its header table. The page shows it, and
  the [recipe directory](recipes/directory.qmd) counts it.
- **Top-10 collections are generated views** — OWASP ML/LLM/API Top-10
  recipe sets render as generated index pages over recipe tags. The
  collections never re-organise the book. See the [recipe
  directory](recipes/directory.qmd) for the current coverage.
- **Recipes are technical and grounded** — every command quotes the
  manifest row (the single source of truth), the landed CLI slice, or
  the pinned upstream source. Expected outputs render as shapes, never
  invented transcripts. The mlflow pair recipe runs the landed
  `kailash-integration-mlflow-attack` probe pair (see
  [Attack the platform, then verify](recipes/attack-defence/attack-then-verify.qmd)).

## Status

The project builds the book in the 2026.01 release window. Wave 1
landed the recipe template, the organisation ADR, the worked exemplar
(garak), and grounded core setup pages. Wave 2 is in build. It adds
the deep recipe set across all sections, header tables on every page,
code-block spacing, and the directory generator. The repository's
issue tracker tracks progress (cookbook parent: the repo's pinned
issue; wave 2: KA-WS-5.12).
